newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close lower in mixed trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close lower in mixed trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Wednesday in what traders described as a technical correction after a sharp rise since the beginning of the year.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.69 percent, or 1.69 points, to 241.64 on all-share turnover of 145 million shekels against 148 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.88 percent lower at 250.99.

"The long awaited correction finaly came although we were hoping for a much stronger move. The market has been trying for the last several days to go through a correction but it did not succeed," said Michael Politzer, head of the economic department at Zeller Eblagon Securities.
Traders said that from a technical prespective the correction was a healthy step.
"Investors were taking profits today but towards the end of the trading day the trend changed and the market closed with only a mild decline," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"I believe that on Thursday the positive momentum will continue," he said.
"The market has to relax. It rose 20 percent in three weeks and now it has to stabilise and wait for fresh news before it can rise again," Politzer said.

Bank Leumi fell 2.25 percent to 505 agorot. On Wednesday, Bank Leumi said the Israeli government company charged with selling the state's bank shares told it to prepare a prospectus for the sale of a 10 percent stake in Tel Aviv.
Based on the bank's current market valuation, the offering will be for about 720 million shekels.

Ackerstein Industries rose 2.5 percent to 493 agorot after it was rated a buy on Wednesday by Bank Hapoalim economists who said the construction products company was undervalued by more than 30 percent.
A report issued by the bank's research department estimated Ackerstein's real value at between $56 million and $62 million as opposed to its market value of around $43 million.

The most active shares were Israel Chemicals, which rose 1.75 percent to 352 agorot on turnover of 12.8 million shekels, and Supersol, which fell 0.25 percent to 875 agorot on volume of 5.8 million shekels.

The third active share was Koor Industries which closed unchanged at 33,140 agorot. The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that Egypt's Kato Industries plans to buy a substantial stake in Koor this month, forming a strategic link in support of Middle East peace efforts. Koor declined comment.
